paragraphs.title: Zophar's Answer and the Brief Joy of the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Zophar the Naamathite answered.
Verse 5 says that the hypocrite's joy is only for a moment.
easy.q: How long does the joy of the hypocrite last?

easy.explanation: Zophar says that his thoughts cause him to answer and that the spirit of his understanding answers him.
easy.q: What does Zophar claim will cause him to answer?

answers: A conclusion or reason for his answer
The beginning of a new journey
medium.explanation: “Therefore” connects Zophar's thoughts and understanding with his decision to answer.
medium.q: What does the word “Therefore” show in Zophar's speech?

answers: A rebuke that provokes a response
medium.explanation: Zophar has heard Job's reproving words, and they cause him to answer.
medium.q: In verse 3, what does “the check of my reproach” mean in context?

answers: To say that the teaching is ancient and familiar
To describe the creation of heaven
medium.explanation: He presents the short triumph of the wicked as an old and widely known truth.
medium.q: Why does Zophar refer to what has been known “since man was placed upon earth”?

answers: Between the wicked person's apparent triumph and its brief duration
challenge.explanation: Zophar says that the wicked may appear to triumph, but that triumph is short.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in Zophar's words?

answers: The wicked person's success will soon end
The wicked triumph only inside a house
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the wicked person's apparent success is temporary.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “the triumphing of the wicked is short”?

answers: Through an ancient and generally known understanding
challenge.explanation: He appeals to knowledge that has been recognized since humanity was placed on earth.
challenge.q: How does Zophar present the authority of his teaching?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Person's Disappearance and the End of His Greatness

answers: To the depths of the sea
To the heavens, with his head reaching the clouds
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that his excellency may mount up to the heavens and his head reach the clouds.
easy.q: How high may the wicked person's excellency rise?

answers: A dream and a vision of the night
easy.explanation: Verses 8–9 compare his disappearance to a dream and a night vision.
easy.q: What is the wicked person's disappearance compared to?

answers: In the dust with his youthful strength
On a throne over his children
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that his bones lie down with him in the dust.
easy.q: Where will the wicked person lie at the end?

answers: The higher he rises, the more certain his disappearance
medium.explanation: Even if he rises to the heavens, he will perish and vanish.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the wicked person's height and his fate?

answers: A request for directions to his house
medium.explanation: The question shows that those who saw him can no longer find him.
medium.q: In the phrase “they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?”, what does “Where is he?” express?

answers: Something fleeting that cannot be found afterward
medium.explanation: A dream or vision disappears quickly and cannot be recovered after it is gone.
medium.q: What does the comparison to a dream or night vision emphasize?

answers: To emphasize the speed and completeness of his disappearance
challenge.explanation: The comparisons to dung, a dream, and a vision all stress that he will vanish completely.
challenge.q: Why does the passage use several images for the wicked person's disappearance?

answers: The wicked person has become more famous
No clear trace of his presence remains
challenge.explanation: The question expresses wonder because the person who was seen can no longer be found.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the question “Where is he?”

answers: They will seek to restore what was taken from the poor
They will increase their father's wealth
challenge.explanation: His children will seek to please the poor and restore their goods.
challenge.q: What will happen to the wicked person's children according to verse 10?

paragraphs.title: Hidden Evil and Wealth Taken Away

answers: In his mouth and under his tongue
easy.explanation: Verses 12–13 say that he keeps wickedness in his mouth and under his tongue.
easy.q: Where does the wicked person hide wickedness?

easy.explanation: Verse 14 says that his meat becomes the gall of asps within him.
easy.q: What does his meat become in his bowels?

answers: He will give them to the poor willingly
He will vomit them up, and God will cast them out
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that he will vomit up the riches and that God will cast them out of his belly.
easy.q: What will happen to the riches he swallowed?

medium.explanation: Asps are poisonous snakes, so their gall represents deadly poison.
medium.q: What are “asps” in the phrase “the gall of asps”?

answers: It turns into poison within him
medium.explanation: Although he keeps wickedness sweet in his mouth, it becomes poisonous within him.
medium.q: What is the relationship between hiding wickedness in the mouth and what happens inside the body?

answers: He will hold it only temporarily
He will increase it through honest labor
medium.explanation: The wealth will be taken from him, and he will not enjoy what he acquired.
medium.q: What do these verses teach about the wealth the wicked person obtained?

answers: Both may seem desirable but bring a destructive result
challenge.explanation: The evil and wealth he takes in do not remain beneficial; they become harmful or are removed.
challenge.q: What symbolic connection is made between poison and riches?

answers: He will not enjoy abundance and pleasant prosperity
He will discover rivers of food
He will move to another land
challenge.explanation: The verse denies him the enjoyment of rich and pleasant abundance.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter”?

answers: He swallowed it, but cannot keep it
challenge.explanation: The riches are pictured as swallowed, but God causes them to be expelled.
challenge.q: How is the wicked person's relationship to his wealth described?

paragraphs.title: Oppression of the Poor and the Coming Troubles

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says that he oppressed and forsook the poor.
easy.q: Whom does the wicked person oppress?

answers: A house he did not build
easy.explanation: The verse says that he violently took away a house which he did not build.
easy.q: What did he violently take away?

answers: God casts the fury of His wrath upon him
easy.explanation: Verse 23 says that God casts His fury upon him while he is eating.
easy.q: What happens when the wicked person is ready to fill his belly?

medium.explanation: Quietness means peace or rest, which the wicked person does not possess.
medium.q: What does “quietness” mean in “he shall not feel quietness in his belly”?

answers: His greed and oppression leave him inwardly restless
He has no food at all
medium.explanation: His possessions and desires do not give him inner peace.
medium.q: Why does the wicked person not feel quietness within him?

answers: He faces trouble because of his wrongdoing
medium.explanation: His oppression and robbery are followed by distress and judgment.
medium.q: What is the result of his treatment of the poor and the houses he took?

answers: The wicked person reaches fullness but does not have peace
The wicked person is poor but joyful
The poor are rich and the wicked person helps them
challenge.explanation: Although he has abundance, he has no quietness and is overtaken by trouble.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in these verses?

answers: Trouble and hostile force will come against him from every side
He will work for the poor
challenge.explanation: The expression portrays distress coming upon him from all directions.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “every hand of the wicked shall come upon him”?

challenge.explanation: Verse 23 says that God casts the fury of His wrath upon him.
challenge.q: Who sends the fury described in the final verse of this section?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Person Pursued and Judged

easy.explanation: Verse 24 says that he shall flee from the iron weapon.
easy.q: From what does the wicked person flee?

easy.explanation: Verse 26 says that a fire not blown shall consume what remains in his tabernacle.
easy.q: What will consume the remnant in his tabernacle?

answers: The portion and heritage appointed to him by God
easy.explanation: Verse 29 calls this the portion and heritage appointed to the wicked person by God.
easy.q: What is the wicked person's portion?

answers: Gifts are being given to him
medium.explanation: The word “terrors” refers to frightening dangers that come upon him.
medium.q: What does “terrors are upon him” mean?

answers: The bow of steel strikes him
medium.explanation: Verse 24 says that the bow of steel shall strike him through.
medium.q: What happens when the wicked person flees from the iron weapon?

answers: Heaven reveals his sin and the earth rises against him
medium.explanation: Verse 27 describes both heaven revealing his iniquity and the earth rising against him.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the revelation of his iniquity and the earth's response?

answers: That the wicked person has many escape routes
That judgment pursues him from every side
That he is protected from danger
challenge.explanation: Each attempted escape leads to another threat, and even his household is consumed.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of weapons, terrors, and fire emphasize?

answers: Hidden troubles are reserved for his secret places
He finds a safe place in the darkness
challenge.explanation: The darkness represents concealed judgment and danger awaiting him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “All darkness shall be hid in his secret places”?

answers: With his victory over his enemies
With the declaration that this is his portion and heritage from God
challenge.explanation: The final verse identifies his judgment as the portion and heritage appointed to him by God.
challenge.q: How does the description of the wicked person's fate end?

short_answers.question: According to verse 5, how long is the joy of the hypocrite?
short_answers.explanation: Job 20:5 says that the hypocrite's joy is only for a moment.

short_answers.question: What does the wicked person swallow in verse 15?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says, “He hath swallowed down riches,” but God will cause him to vomit them up.

short_answers.question: What does heaven reveal in verse 27?
short_answers.explanation: Job 20:27 says, “The heaven shall reveal his iniquity.”
